data.title: Stock Today: Zetrix AI Rallies 16.67% After RM130 Million MYEG Ventures Clarification
data.description:
Zetrix AI Bhd shares jumped 16.67% to RM0.280 as of 10.44 am, rebounding after trading in the counter was suspended the previous day following a Bursa Malaysia query over its proposed RM130 million acquisition of a 50% stake in MYEG Ventures Inc.

The stock opened at RM0.245 and climbed as high as RM0.290 before easing to RM0.280. It had closed at RM0.240 previously, giving it a gain of RM0.040.

Trading activity was also brisk, with 549.33 million shares changing hands. The counter recorded a low of RM0.245, while the buy price stood at RM0.280 and sell price at RM0.285.

The strong rebound came after Zetrix AI clarified that the acquisition would raise its effective interest in MYEG Philippines Inc to 74.5%, comprising its existing 49% direct stake and a 25.5% indirect interest through MYEG Ventures.

Zetrix AI had earlier incorrectly stated that MYEG Ventures held 60% of MYEG Philippines, before correcting the figure to 51%.

The proposed acquisition involves 15.25 million MYEG Ventures shares, representing the seller’s entire 50% stake. Zetrix AI said the RM130 million consideration would be funded through a combination of new shares and cash.

The company plans to issue up to 360.57 million new ordinary shares, with the issue price to be determined based on the five-day volume-weighted average market price immediately before issuance.

data.title: Asia Markets: Nikkei, KOSPI And Chinese Stocks Climb Ahead Of Payrolls
data.description:
Asian shares climbed on Friday as investors took comfort from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller’s softer stance on interest rates, while markets turned their attention to the latest US jobs data for clues on the Fed’s next move.

Waller said recent data showed signs of disinflation and that he would favour keeping rates steady at this month’s policy meeting if upcoming reports reinforced that trend. Markets subsequently cut the implied probability of a September rate hike to around 50% from about 63% a day earlier.

“Waller is pushing back against the thrust of the argument made by Warsh last week that there is little evidence that underlying inflation has moved lower,” analysts at JPMorgan said in a note.

“We believe that Chair Warsh will deliver a hike if he advocates for it. Absent his advocacy, Governor Waller’s speech reinforces our view that the bar for data to sway the data-dependent majority to hike this month remains elevated.”

The MSCI Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan rose 1%, while Japan’s Nikkei gained 0.8%. Chinese blue-chip stocks climbed 1% and South Korea’s KOSPI advanced 1.1%.

Attention now turns to US nonfarm payrolls, with economists expecting 56,000 jobs to have been added in August after a surprise fall of 23,000 in July. The unemployment rate is expected to remain at 4.1%.

The softer US rate outlook also eased pressure on bonds, with two-year Treasury yields holding at 4.3381% after falling overnight. Ten-year yields stood at 4.7620%.

Meanwhile, the dollar remained under pressure at 98.96 against major currencies, while the yen strengthened to around 155.70 per dollar as traders increased bets on a BOJ rate hike this month.

Reuters

data.title: Bursa In The Red At Midday As Investors Lock In Gains
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia remained lower at midday on Friday as investors took profit following recent gains, with selling pressure particularly evident in industrial products, plantation and financial stocks.

At 12:30pm, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 8.11 points or 0.47% to 1,707.02 from Thursday’s close of 1,715.13. The index opened 1.39 points lower at 1,713.74.

Market breadth remained negative, with 569 decliners against 419 gainers, while 527 counters were unchanged. Another 1,257 counters were not traded and 19 were suspended.

Trading volume stood at 2.75 billion shares worth RM1.50 billion.

Apex Securities Bhd said the technology sector could remain in focus following Nvidia’s US$12.9 billion AI partnership with Hugging Face, which lifted sentiment across semiconductor-related stocks.

The research house also highlighted the energy sector as Brent crude continued trading above US$95 a barrel amid rising tensions in the Gulf region. Construction stocks could also benefit from continued AI and data centre investments driving demand for related infrastructure and construction works.

Among heavyweights, CIMB Group gained one sen to RM8.00 while Maybank and Tenaga Nasional fell four sen each to RM10.54 and RM13.64 respectively. Public Bank declined two sen to RM4.98 and IHH Healthcare eased one sen to RM7.98.

Zetrix AI was the most actively traded counter, rising 3.5 sen to 27.5 sen, followed by Salutica which gained 4.5 sen to 16 sen.

On the broader market, the FBM ACE Index rose 24.86 points to 5,212.52 while the FBM Emas Index fell 60.64 points to 12,622.70. The Financial Services Index declined 56.84 points and the Plantation Index shed 120.03 points.

data.title: Stock Today: Kerjaya Prospek Gains 3.25% As Data Centre Deal Boosts Sentiment
data.description:
Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd shares rose 3.25% to RM3.18 as of 11.56 am, with the construction counter extending its gains following news of its record RM858 million data centre contract in Johor.

The stock opened at RM3.08 and climbed to an intraday high of RM3.18, while its lowest level was RM3.07. It was up RM0.10 from its previous close of RM3.08.

Trading volume stood at 820,600 shares, with 178 lots on the buy queue at RM3.17 against 480 lots offered at RM3.18.

The latest movement comes after RHB Research maintained its BUY call on Kerjaya Prospek but raised its target price to RM3.87 from RM3.41, implying 34% upside.

The research house said the RM858 million data centre contract, its largest single project to date, represents around 15% of Kerjaya Prospek’s RM5.9 billion outstanding order book.

The contract involves mechanical, electrical and plumbing fit-out works at a data centre in Iskandar Puteri and is expected to start in the third quarter of 2026, with completion targeted within eight months.

The award has brought Kerjaya Prospek’s FY26 contract wins to RM3.2 billion, already above RHB’s previous full-year target of RM2.8 billion. RHB has raised its FY26 job replenishment assumption to RM3.5 billion and sees another RM200 million to RM300 million in potential wins for the remainder of the year.

RHB also raised its earnings forecasts for FY26, FY27 and FY28 by 3%, 6% and 3% respectively, citing stronger contract replenishment and growing exposure to industrial projects including data centres.

data.title: Stock Today: Press Metal Rises 0.75% On Positive Aluminium Outlook
data.description:
Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd shares rose 0.75% to RM8.03 as of 3:58pm on Friday, as investors continued to weigh the group’s outlook against a positive view from RHB Research on the aluminium market.

The counter opened at RM7.90 and climbed to an intraday high of RM8.05 before settling at RM8.03. It had closed at RM7.97 previously, while the day’s low stood at RM7.90.

Trading volume stood at 1.80 million shares, with the stock quoted at RM8.02 on the buy side and RM8.03 on the sell side.

The gain comes after RHB Research maintained its OVERWEIGHT call on the basic materials sector, with Press Metal remaining its top pick as a structural aluminium supply deficit is expected to keep prices elevated.

RHB expects the aluminium market to remain in a deficit of around 900,000 to one million tonnes in 2026, while demand recorded a marginal year-on-year improvement in the first half of the year.

The research house also expects Press Metal to deliver stronger results in 2H26, supported by the lag in aluminium pricing, lower alumina and logistics costs and a higher Main Japanese Ports premium contracted at US$395 per tonne.

RHB maintained its aluminium price assumptions at US$3,250 per tonne for 2026 and US$3,050 for 2027, noting that the year-to-date average of US$3,329 was around 2% above its 2026 assumption.

Longer term, RHB sees Press Metal’s 80%-owned Kalimantan Alumina Nusantara project as a major catalyst, with commissioning scheduled for 2Q27. Once expanded, the project could lift the group’s alumina self-sufficiency to almost 100%, potentially supporting a material improvement in smelting margins.

RHB believes the combination of elevated aluminium prices and structural supply tightness could justify a re-rating of Press Metal above its historical mean.

data.title: Volkswagen Jumps 7% As Historic Restructuring Deal Wins Investor Backing
data.description:
Volkswagen shares jumped 7% in early Frankfurt trading after the automaker reached a major turnaround agreement that eased tensions with unions and shareholder Lower Saxony.

The agreement, approved by Volkswagen’s supervisory board late Thursday, marks the biggest restructuring in the company’s 89-year history and includes a further 50,000 job cuts, bringing total planned reductions across the group to 100,000.

The deal also leaves the future of four German plants undecided, while averting a potential escalation between management, unions and Lower Saxony, which together hold a majority of seats on Volkswagen’s supervisory board.

Management had previously considered calling a shareholder meeting to push through its restructuring demands, which would have marked an unprecedented escalation of the conflict.

“The agreement … is a positive sign for Volkswagen and the capital market – even if it involves severe cutbacks amongst the workforce and within the group,” said Moritz Kronenberger of Volkswagen shareholder Union Investment.

“The ball is now entirely in the Executive Board’s court. There are no more excuses,” he said.

Volkswagen is attempting to improve profitability as it faces pressure from US import tariffs, a stagnant European market and aggressive Chinese competitors.

These pressures have weighed on the group’s operating margin, which stood at just 3.8% in the first half of the year.

Reuters

data.title: Gold Pushes Past US$4,500, RHB Maintains Bullish Bias
data.description:
Gold prices held steady on Friday after jumping 2% in the previous session, with investors awaiting US payrolls data for clues on the Federal Reserve’s next interest rate move, while RHB Research maintained its bullish outlook on the precious metal.

Spot gold stood at US$4,469.26 per ounce as of 6:33am GMT, heading for a modest weekly gain. US gold futures for December delivery fell 0.5% to US$4,515.70.

The gains on Thursday came as traders scaled back expectations of a September rate hike after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would support leaving rates unchanged if inflation pressures continued to moderate.

Markets are currently pricing in around a 50% chance of a Fed rate hike later this month, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. The US nonfarm payrolls report is due later on Friday.

RHB Research said COMEX gold had broken through the US$4,500 resistance level after closing at US$4,504.90 on Thursday, supported by accelerating bullish momentum.

The research house maintained its long position, noting that the upward-trending relative strength index (RSI) and rising 20- and 50-day simple moving averages continue to support the bullish technical setup.

RHB expects gold to test the next resistance at US$4,700, followed by US$4,900, while immediate support is seen at US$4,300 and US$4,150.

The research house advised traders to maintain long positions initiated at US$4,273.30, with a stop-loss at US$4,300.

Meanwhile, Reuters reported that weaker payrolls and a rise in unemployment could weaken the case for a rate hike and provide further support for gold. Elevated interest rates generally weigh on the non-yielding asset, while continued central bank demand could limit any downside.

data.title: Oil Falls As Iran Talks Raise Hopes Of Strait Of Hormuz Reopening
data.description:
Oil prices slipped on Thursday as progress in Iran-Oman talks raised hopes of a potential US-Iran peace deal that could eventually reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while fresh US inventory data added pressure to prices.

Brent crude futures fell 37 US cents or 0.5% to US$79.08 a barrel by 0024 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate declined 53 US cents or 0.7% to US$74.69. Brent had edged higher in the previous session while WTI finished slightly lower, according to Reuters.

Nomura Securities economist Yuki Takashima said selling pressure emerged after reports that the Iran-Oman talks were making progress, with prices returning to levels seen when the US and Iran reached an interim peace agreement on June 17.

A proposed deal could give Tehran control over ships entering the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian and regional sources cited by Reuters.

However, the US has not commented on the proposal and officials have previously opposed any arrangement that would give Iran control over access to the key energy shipping route.

Concerns over wider regional disruption also remain. Iran-aligned Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi oil tankers, while Takashima said the risk of further attacks on Red Sea shipping was limiting optimism over an end to regional shipping disruptions.

Separately, US crude inventories rose by 2.5 million barrels to 407 million barrels in the week ended July 31, against analysts’ expectations for a 1.5 million-barrel draw, according to the Energy Information Administration.

data.title: HSIF Eyes 26,750 As RHB Sees Bullish Momentum Returning
data.description:
Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) could resume its upward movement after rebounding 76 points in the latest session, with RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) retaining its positive trading bias and long position.

The HSIF closed at 25,910 points after opening at 25,818 points and briefly falling to an intraday low of 25,698 points. It then reversed higher to reach 25,990 points, ending near the session high with a bullish candlestick that erased the previous session’s losses.

RHB said the fresh bullish candlestick and a rising Relative Strength Index above the 50% mark point to improving momentum. The index is also trading firmly above its 20-day and 50-day simple moving average lines, keeping the broader trend tilted towards the bulls.

“If the HSIF sustains above the 20-day SMA line, it is likely to move higher towards the 26,750 pts resistance,” RHB said.

The research house therefore recommended traders maintain the long position initiated at 24,657 points based on the July 15 close. It placed the stop-loss threshold at 23,500 points.

The HSIF’s immediate support is at 24,200 points, followed by 23,500 points, while resistance is seen at 26,000 points and then 26,750 points.

The bullish view comes despite weakness in the evening session, when the index fell 236 points to last trade at 25,674 points.

data.title: US Stocks Continue To Rise After Record Rally
data.description:
US stocks rose modestly on Wednesday after a searing rally, as investors weighed earnings from SpaceX and AMD and President Trump’s comments that a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could happen as early as Wednesday.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4%. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.6% after the indexes closed at record highs

A rise in Asian markets overnight lifted global markets as investors assessed earnings and cheered diplomatic efforts for another peace deal between the US and Iran — no matter how fragile. South Korea’s KOSPI index led gains, rising almost 4%.

SpaceX didn’t receive the Wall Street welcome it was looking for in its first report as a public company. Shares of the Elon Musk-led company dropped 12% after its AI spending overshadowed a second quarter earnings beat. SpaceX stock faces additional pressure this week when 20% of shares will be unlocked for trading.

data.title: Wall Street Splits As Dow Rallies While Tech Stumbles
data.description:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record high on Wednesday as hopes for progress towards a peace deal involving Iran helped support sentiment, although a sell-off in SpaceX and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares pulled the Nasdaq lower.

The Dow rose 263.18 points, or 0.49%, to 54,349.06 while the S&P 500 slipped 13 points, or 0.17%, to 7,723.52. The Nasdaq Composite fell 221.55 points, or 0.83%, to 26,363.44, ending a four-session winning streak.

Markets have been buoyed by hopes of progress towards resolving the conflict with Iran, which has also pushed oil prices and US Treasury yields lower. The resulting easing in inflation concerns has reduced expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September.

“It’s just a straight rocket shot that we’ve gone up, we didn’t even take a breath,” said Kenny Polcari, chief market strategist at Slatestone Wealth in Jupiter, Florida.

“It’s progress, but the market’s just going, we’re not going to give it to you this time until we actually see the progress, because how many times have we been jerked around over the last four months?”

SpaceX was among the biggest drags on the Nasdaq, with shares plunging 13.6% after the Elon Musk-led company reported its first earnings since going public.

Revenue nearly doubled while operating losses narrowed, helped by growth in its Starlink satellite communications and artificial intelligence businesses. However, investors were concerned about the scale of its spending on AI infrastructure, including data centres.

The stock could also face further pressure with its post-IPO lock-up period set to expire from Thursday.

AMD shares also fell 7% despite the chipmaker forecasting quarterly revenue above Wall Street expectations on strong demand for AI-related products. Investors appeared to be looking for clearer evidence that heavy AI infrastructure spending will translate into faster growth.

The Dow, meanwhile, received support from a 4.6% jump in Amgen after the drugmaker reported a 9% increase in second-quarter sales. Eli Lilly rose 4.9% after raising its full-year revenue forecast, helping the S&P 500 healthcare sector gain 1.3%.

Disney also contributed to the Dow’s gains, with its shares rising 3.6% after the entertainment company beat third-quarter profit expectations.

On the economic front, US private payroll growth slowed in July, according to the ADP national employment report, ahead of the government’s closely watched non-farm payrolls report due on Friday.

The Institute for Supply Management’s non-manufacturing purchasing managers’ index edged up to 54.1 in July from 54.0 in June, although it came in below economists’ forecast of 54.5. A reading above 50 still indicates expansion.

Investors remain focused on inflation and the Federal Reserve’s next move, with the market now pricing a 54.9% chance of a rate hike at the September meeting, down from 58.3% a week earlier.

Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said in an interview with CNBC that he believed it was time to begin slowly raising interest rates, while Federal Reserve Board Governor Lisa Cook and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly were also scheduled to speak later in the day.

data.title: Asian Stocks Retreat As Tech Rally Cools, Iran Talks Stay In Focus
data.description:
Asian shares retreated on Thursday as technology stocks pulled back after an AI-driven rally, while investors kept an eye on developments surrounding a potential Iran peace deal and the upcoming US jobs report.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 0.69%, led by a 3.64% slide in South Korean shares and a 1.57% decline in Japan’s Nikkei. Samsung Electronics dropped 2.44%, while SK Hynix fell 6.95%. In Tokyo, Kioxia plunged 9.61% and Tokyo Electron declined 4.61%.

The pullback followed a weaker Wall Street session, with the Nasdaq ending a multi-day winning streak after investors remained cautious over lofty expectations for technology companies. Advanced Micro Devices fell despite beating analysts’ estimates, while concerns also emerged over the scale of data centre investment.

Oil prices remained relatively steady as markets assessed prospects for a deal involving Iran and Oman that could help reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude slipped 0.18% to US$79.31 a barrel while US West Texas Intermediate fell 0.35% to US$74.96.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia senior geo-economics analyst Madison Cartwright said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be reached by early September, although he remained sceptical that an agreement was imminent.

Meanwhile, investors are turning towards Friday’s US non-farm payrolls report after ADP data showed private employers added just 44,000 jobs in July, below expectations. Futures markets now price a 54% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September, down from 58% a day earlier.

Reuters

data.title: Dollar Lingers Near Six-Week Low, Yen Gives Up Ground
data.description:
The US dollar remained near a six-week low while the Japanese yen eased on Thursday as traders awaited further developments on a proposed US-Iran deal and Friday’s US jobs report for clues on the Federal Reserve’s next interest rate move.

The yen was 0.1% weaker at 157.88 per US dollar, giving back some of the gains following Japan’s recent intervention. It had strengthened to 155.20 on Monday but remains well above its multi-decade low of almost 164 reached in July.

The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six major peers, edged 0.1% higher to 99.76 after hitting a six-week low on Monday.

The euro was steady at US$1.1544 while sterling slipped 0.1% to US$1.3454. The Australian dollar fell 0.2% to US$0.7039 while the New Zealand dollar was also down 0.2% at US$0.5873.

Markets remained focused on developments around the Strait of Hormuz after a proposed deal between Iran and Oman was reported to potentially give Tehran control over inbound traffic through the strategic waterway.

There was no immediate US comment on the proposal, while President Donald Trump has said a deal to reopen the strait was imminent. US officials have repeatedly said Washington would not accept Iranian control over access to the key energy shipping route.

Brent crude was steady at around US$79.50 a barrel, close to levels last seen when the US and Iran reached an interim peace agreement in June.

Investors are now turning towards Friday’s US non-farm payrolls report, which could provide further clues on the Fed’s interest rate path after the central bank left rates unchanged last month.

A Reuters poll expects US employers to have added 80,000 jobs in July, up from 57,000 in June, while the unemployment rate is forecast to remain at 4.2%.

A stronger jobs reading could support the dollar by strengthening expectations of a September rate hike, while a weaker report could reinforce expectations that the Fed will keep rates unchanged.
